problem: Find the $x$-coordinate of the point on the curve $y=\sqrt{x-2}+2$ that is closest to the point $(3,2).$

Find the $y$-coordinate of the point on the curve $y=-{x}^{2}+6x$ that is closest to the point $(3,0).$ Do not round the answer.

{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
Let us consider the *squared* distance $S$ between $(3,0)$ and a general point $P(x,y)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =(x-3)^{2}+(y-0)^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}-6x+9+{y}^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}-6x+{y}^{2}+9\end{aligned}
$$

We require that the point $P$ lies on the curve $y=-{x}^{2}+6x.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}S(y) & =-y+{y}^{2}+9 \\  & ={y}^{2}-y+9.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the minimum distance, we take the first derivative of $S(y)$ and equate it to zero. This gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}^{′}(y)=2y-1 & =0 \\ 2y & =1 \\ y & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We can see that ${S}^{″}(y)=2>0.$ Therefore, $y=\frac{1}{2}$ is a minimum of $S.$

So, the squared distance (and therefore the actual distance) is minimized when $y=\frac{1}{2}.$
